source.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע בֶּן־שָׁא֗וּל כִּ֣י מֵ֤ת אַבְנֵר֙ בְּחֶבְר֔וֹן וַיִּרְפּ֖וּ יָדָ֑יו וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל נִבְהָֽלוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And heard [the] son of Saul that had died Abner in Hebron, and dropped his hands, and all Israel were dismayed.

en.L: And the son of Saul heard that Abner had died in Hebron, and his hands went slack, and all Israel was dismayed.
en.B: When Saul's son heard that Abner had died in Hebron, he lost heart, and all Israel was alarmed.
en.R: Saul's son Ish-bosheth heard that Abner had died in Hebron. Then he lost all his courage, and all the people of Israel were alarmed.

es.L: Y oyó el hijo de Saúl que Abner había muerto en Hebrón, y se le aflojaron las manos, y todo Israel se turbó.
es.B: Cuando el hijo de Saúl oyó que Abner había muerto en Hebrón, perdió el ánimo, y todo Israel se alarmó.
es.R: Isboset, el hijo de Saúl, oyó que Abner había muerto en Hebrón. Entonces perdió todo su valor, y todo el pueblo de Israel se alarmó.

fr.L: Et le fils de Saül apprit qu’Abner était mort à Hébron, et ses mains faiblirent, et tout Israël fut consterné.
fr.B: Quand le fils de Saül apprit qu’Abner était mort à Hébron, il perdit courage, et tout Israël fut saisi d’inquiétude.
fr.R: Ishbosheth, le fils de Saül, a appris qu’Abner était mort à Hébron. Alors il a perdu tout son courage, et tout le peuple d’Israël a pris peur.

sw.L: Mwana wa Sauli akasikia kwamba Abneri amekufa huko Hebroni, mikono yake ikalegea, na Israeli wote wakafadhaika.
sw.B: Mwana wa Sauli aliposikia kwamba Abneri amekufa huko Hebroni, alikata tamaa, na Israeli wote wakaingiwa na hofu.
sw.R: Ishboshethi mwana wa Sauli alisikia kwamba Abneri amekufa huko Hebroni. Akapoteza ujasiri wake wote, na watu wote wa Israeli wakaingiwa na hofu.

vi.L: Con trai Sau-lơ nghe rằng Áp-ne đã chết tại Hếp-rôn thì tay rụng rời, và cả Y-sơ-ra-ên đều hoảng sợ.
vi.B: Khi con trai Sau-lơ nghe Áp-ne đã chết tại Hếp-rôn, ông mất hết can đảm, và cả Y-sơ-ra-ên đều hoang mang.
vi.R: Ích-bô-sết, con trai Sau-lơ, nghe tin Áp-ne đã chết tại Hếp-rôn. Ông mất hết tinh thần, và toàn dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đều hoảng sợ.

decisions.choice: the son of Saul: the Hebrew text does not give his name here
alternatives: Mephibosheth son of Saul (ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "the son of Saul". The ancient Greek translation adds a name, calling him Mephibosheth, the name it uses for Ish-bosheth in this chapter. The man meant is Ish-bosheth, Saul's son, whom Abner had made king over Israel (2:8-10; 4:5). The Hebrew is followed; reviewers should check the Greek evidence.

decisions.choice: his hands dropped: his courage and strength failed
decisions.reason: Hands that hang limp picture a man who has lost the will to act (Isaiah 13:7; Jeremiah 6:24; Zephaniah 3:16).

decisions.choice: Abner's death left Ish-bosheth's kingdom without its real leader
decisions.reason: Abner had made Ish-bosheth king and held the power behind him (2:8-9; 3:6, 11). He had also begun to bring the northern tribes over to David (3:12-21) before Joab killed him at Hebron (3:27). "All Israel" is the kingdom of Ish-bosheth, set against Judah, as in chapter 2.

decisions.choice: Saul's son Ish-bosheth
decisions.reason: Readable names the son, as verse 5 does, so that a new reader knows who is meant.

decisions.choice: lost heart (Balanced); lost all his courage (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the picture of limp hands means. Literal keeps the picture.

decisions.choice: "tay rụng rời" (L); "mất hết can đảm" (B); "mất hết tinh thần" (R)
decisions.reason: His courage failed (meaning decision); Vietnamese "rụng rời tay chân" is itself a picture of fear, so Literal keeps the hands.

source.text: וּשְׁנֵ֣י אֲנָשִׁ֣ים שָׂרֵֽי־גְדוּדִ֣ים הָי֪וּ בֶן־שָׁא֟וּל שֵׁם֩ הָאֶחָ֨ד בַּֽעֲנָ֜ה וְשֵׁ֧ם הַשֵּׁנִ֣י רֵכָ֗ב בְּנֵ֛י רִמּ֥וֹן הַבְּאֶֽרֹתִ֖י מִבְּנֵ֣י בִנְיָמִ֑ן כִּ֚י גַּם־בְּאֵר֔וֹת תֵּחָשֵׁ֖ב עַל־בִּנְיָמִֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And two men, commanders of raiding bands, were [to the] son of Saul; [the] name of the one [was] Baanah, and [the] name of the second [was] Rechab, sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, from [the] sons of Benjamin; for also Beeroth is reckoned to Benjamin.

en.L: And Saul's son had two men, commanders of raiding bands; the name of the one [was] Baanah, and the name of the second [was] Rechab, sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, of the sons of Benjamin; for Beeroth too is counted as [part of] Benjamin.
en.B: Saul's son had two men who were commanders of raiding bands. One was called Baanah and the other Rechab, and both were sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, from the tribe of Benjamin, since Beeroth also is counted as part of Benjamin.
en.R: Ish-bosheth had two commanders of raiding parties. Their names were Baanah and Rechab. They were sons of Rimmon from the town of Beeroth, in the tribe of Benjamin. (Beeroth is counted as part of Benjamin.)

es.L: Y el hijo de Saúl tenía dos hombres, jefes de bandas de saqueo; el nombre de uno [era] Baaná, y el nombre del segundo [era] Recab, hijos de Rimón el beerotita, de los hijos de Benjamín; porque también Beerot se cuenta [como parte] de Benjamín.
es.B: El hijo de Saúl tenía dos hombres que eran jefes de bandas de asalto. Uno se llamaba Baaná y el otro Recab, y ambos eran hijos de Rimón el beerotita, de la tribu de Benjamín, ya que Beerot también se considera parte de Benjamín.
es.R: Isboset tenía dos jefes de grupos de asalto. Se llamaban Baaná y Recab. Eran hijos de Rimón, del pueblo de Beerot, de la tribu de Benjamín. (Beerot se considera parte de Benjamín).

fr.L: Et le fils de Saül avait deux hommes, chefs de bandes ; le nom de l’un [était] Baana, et le nom du second [était] Rékab, fils de Rimmôn le Béérothite, d’entre les fils de Benjamin ; car Béeroth aussi est comptée comme [faisant partie de] Benjamin.
fr.B: Le fils de Saül avait à son service deux hommes, chefs de bandes armées. L’un s’appelait Baana et l’autre Rékab ; ils étaient fils de Rimmôn le Béérothite, de la tribu de Benjamin, car Béeroth est aussi comptée comme faisant partie de Benjamin.
fr.R: Ishbosheth avait deux chefs de groupes armés qui faisaient des attaques. Ils s’appelaient Baana et Rékab. C’étaient des fils de Rimmôn, de la ville de Béeroth, dans la tribu de Benjamin. (Béeroth est comptée comme une ville de Benjamin.)

sw.L: Mwana wa Sauli alikuwa na watu wawili, wakuu wa vikosi vya wavamizi; jina la mmoja [lilikuwa] Baana, na jina la wa pili [lilikuwa] Rekabu, wana wa Rimoni Mbeerothi, wa wana wa Benyamini; kwa maana Beerothi pia inahesabiwa [kuwa sehemu ya] Benyamini.
sw.B: Mwana wa Sauli alikuwa na watu wawili waliokuwa wakuu wa vikosi vya wavamizi. Mmoja aliitwa Baana na mwingine Rekabu, nao wote wawili walikuwa wana wa Rimoni Mbeerothi, wa kabila la Benyamini, kwa kuwa Beerothi nayo inahesabiwa kuwa sehemu ya Benyamini.
sw.R: Ishboshethi alikuwa na wakuu wawili wa vikundi vya wavamizi. Majina yao yalikuwa Baana na Rekabu. Walikuwa wana wa Rimoni kutoka mji wa Beerothi, katika kabila la Benyamini. (Beerothi inahesabiwa kuwa sehemu ya Benyamini.)

vi.L: Con trai Sau-lơ có hai người làm chỉ huy các toán quân đột kích; tên của người thứ nhất là Ba-a-na, và tên của người thứ hai là Rê-cáp, con trai của Rim-môn người Bê-ê-rốt, thuộc con cháu Bên-gia-min; vì Bê-ê-rốt cũng được kể [thuộc về] Bên-gia-min.
vi.B: Con trai Sau-lơ có hai người làm chỉ huy các toán quân đột kích. Một người tên là Ba-a-na, người kia tên là Rê-cáp. Cả hai là con trai của Rim-môn người Bê-ê-rốt, thuộc chi tộc Bên-gia-min, vì Bê-ê-rốt cũng được kể là thuộc về Bên-gia-min.
vi.R: Ích-bô-sết có hai người chỉ huy các toán quân đi đánh cướp. Tên họ là Ba-a-na và Rê-cáp. Họ là con trai của Rim-môn, người thị trấn Bê-ê-rốt, thuộc chi tộc Bên-gia-min. (Bê-ê-rốt được kể là một phần của Bên-gia-min.)

decisions.choice: commanders of raiding bands: leaders of small fighting troops that made raids
decisions.reason: A *gedud* is a band of fighters sent out on raids (1 Samuel 30:8, 15; 2 Samuel 3:22). These two men led such bands in the service of Ish-bosheth.

decisions.choice: Beeroth: one of the Gibeonite towns, counted as part of Benjamin
decisions.reason: Beeroth was one of the four towns of the Gibeonites who made peace with Joshua (Joshua 9:17), and it was given to Benjamin (Joshua 18:25). The note makes clear that the two killers were Benjaminites, of Saul's own tribe, so the king's murderers came from his own people.

decisions.choice: commanders
decisions.reason: A *sar* in a military setting is a "commander" at every level. Readable says "raiding parties" for "raiding bands".

decisions.choice: the note about Beeroth in parentheses; Ish-bosheth named
decisions.reason: Readable sets the explanation about Beeroth apart, since it is a note by the writer, and names Saul's son as in verse 1.

decisions.choice: "Baaná", "Recab", "Rimón el beerotita", "Beerot"
decisions.reason: Names in their usual Spanish forms, kept the same through both books.

decisions.choice: "Ba-a-na", "Rê-cáp", "Rim-môn", "Bê-ê-rốt", "Ghi-tha-im" (verse 3)
decisions.reason: Names not in the terms note's table, given the usual Protestant forms and kept through the book.

source.text: וַיִּבְרְח֥וּ הַבְּאֵרֹתִ֖ים גִּתָּ֑יְמָה וַֽיִּהְיוּ־שָׁ֣ם גָּרִ֔ים עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And fled the Beerothites to Gittaim, and they have been there sojourning until the day the this.

en.L: And the Beerothites fled to Gittaim and have been sojourners there to this day.
en.B: The Beerothites had fled to Gittaim, and they have lived there as outsiders to this day.
en.R: The people of Beeroth had run away to Gittaim. They have lived there as outsiders to this day.

es.L: Y huyeron los beerotitas a Gitaim, y han vivido allí como inmigrantes hasta el día de hoy.
es.B: Los beerotitas habían huido a Gitaim, y han vivido allí como extranjeros hasta el día de hoy.
es.R: La gente de Beerot había huido a Gitaim. Han vivido allí como extranjeros hasta el día de hoy.

fr.L: Et les Béérothites s’enfuirent à Guittaïm, et ils y ont été des immigrés jusqu’à ce jour.
fr.B: Les Béérothites s’étaient enfuis à Guittaïm, et ils y vivent en étrangers jusqu’à ce jour.
fr.R: Les habitants de Béeroth s’étaient enfuis à Guittaïm. Ils y vivent comme des étrangers jusqu’à aujourd’hui.

sw.L: Wabeerothi wakakimbilia Gittaimu, nao wamekuwa wageni huko mpaka siku hii ya leo.
sw.B: Wabeerothi walikuwa wamekimbilia Gittaimu, nao wameishi huko kama wageni mpaka leo.
sw.R: Watu wa Beerothi walikuwa wamekimbilia Gittaimu. Wameishi huko kama wageni mpaka leo.

vi.L: Người Bê-ê-rốt đã trốn sang Ghi-tha-im và đã sống tại đó làm ngoại kiều cho đến ngày nay.
vi.B: Người Bê-ê-rốt đã trốn sang Ghi-tha-im, và họ sống ở đó như người nơi khác đến cho đến ngày nay.
vi.R: Người Bê-ê-rốt đã chạy trốn sang Ghi-tha-im. Họ sống ở đó như người nơi khác đến cho đến ngày nay.

decisions.choice: the Beerothites had fled: background told from an earlier time
alternatives: the Beerothites fled at the time of the events of this chapter
decisions.reason: The verse explains why men of Beeroth were living elsewhere. When they fled is not said. It may have been when Saul attacked the Gibeonites (21:1-2), or when the Philistines took the land after Saul's defeat (1 Samuel 31:7).

decisions.choice: living as sojourners: residing as outsiders without the rights of the town's own people
decisions.reason: A *ger* lived among a people not his own, without a share of the land. Gittaim is named among the towns of Benjamin after the exile (Nehemiah 11:33).

decisions.choice: to this day: until the time of the writer
decisions.reason: "This day" is the writer's own day, not the time of the story. It shows the account was written down some time after the events.

decisions.choice: sojourners (Literal); outsiders (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: *Ger* is "sojourner" at Literal and "outsider" at Balanced and Readable, as elsewhere. Balanced and Readable say "had fled" because the flight came before the story.

decisions.choice: jusqu'à ce jour (L, B); jusqu'à aujourd'hui (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole of 2 Samuel: "to this day" is the writer's own day (m3), so French keeps it as the writer's phrase rather than a date in the story.

decisions.choice: "làm ngoại kiều" (L); "như người nơi khác đến" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Residing as outsiders without the townspeople's rights (meaning decision); Literal uses the word kept for the sojourner since 1:13, Balanced and Readable describe it.

source.text: וְלִיהֽוֹנָתָן֙ בֶּן־שָׁא֔וּל בֵּ֖ן נְכֵ֣ה רַגְלָ֑יִם בֶּן־חָמֵ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֣ים הָיָ֡ה בְּבֹ֣א שְׁמֻעַת֩ שָׁא֨וּל וִיהֽוֹנָתָ֜ן מִֽיִּזְרְעֶ֗אל וַתִּשָּׂאֵ֤הוּ אֹֽמַנְתּוֹ֙ וַתָּנֹ֔ס וַיְהִ֞י בְּחָפְזָ֥הּ לָנ֛וּס וַיִּפֹּ֥ל וַיִּפָּסֵ֖חַ וּשְׁמ֥וֹ מְפִיבֹֽשֶׁת׃

records.literal_gloss: And to Jonathan son of Saul [was] a son stricken of feet; a son of five years he was in [the] coming of [the] report of Saul and Jonathan from Jezreel, and lifted him his nurse and fled; and it was in her hurrying to flee, and he fell and became lame; and his name [was] Mephibosheth.

en.L: (And Jonathan the son of Saul had a son crippled in [the] feet. He was five years old when the report about Saul and Jonathan came from Jezreel, and his nurse picked him up and fled; and as she hurried to flee, he fell and became lame. And his name [was] Mephibosheth.)
en.B: (Jonathan son of Saul had a son who was lame in both feet. He was five years old when word about Saul and Jonathan arrived from Jezreel. His nurse took him up and fled, but in her haste to get away he fell and was crippled. His name was Mephibosheth.)
en.R: (Saul's son Jonathan had a son whose feet were crippled. He was five years old when the news came from Jezreel that Saul and Jonathan had been killed. His nurse picked him up and ran away. But as she hurried to escape, he fell, and after that he could not walk properly. His name was Mephibosheth.)

es.L: (Y Jonatán hijo de Saúl tenía un hijo lisiado de [los] pies. Tenía cinco años cuando llegó de Jezreel la noticia de Saúl y Jonatán, y su nodriza lo tomó y huyó; y sucedió que, al apresurarse ella para huir, él se cayó y quedó cojo. Y su nombre [era] Mefiboset).
es.B: (Jonatán hijo de Saúl tenía un hijo lisiado de ambos pies. Tenía cinco años cuando llegó de Jezreel la noticia acerca de Saúl y Jonatán. Su nodriza lo tomó y huyó, pero con la prisa por escapar, el niño se cayó y quedó lisiado. Se llamaba Mefiboset).
es.R: (Jonatán, el hijo de Saúl, tenía un hijo que estaba lisiado de los pies. Tenía cinco años cuando llegó de Jezreel la noticia de que habían matado a Saúl y a Jonatán. Su nodriza lo tomó y huyó. Pero con la prisa por escapar, el niño se cayó, y desde entonces no podía caminar bien. Se llamaba Mefiboset).

fr.L: (Et Jonathan, fils de Saül, avait un fils infirme des pieds. Il était fils de cinq ans quand la nouvelle concernant Saül et Jonathan arriva de Jizreël, et sa nourrice le prit et s’enfuit ; et comme elle se hâtait de fuir, il tomba et devint boiteux. Et son nom [était] Mephibosheth.)
fr.B: (Jonathan, fils de Saül, avait un fils infirme des deux pieds. Il avait cinq ans quand la nouvelle concernant Saül et Jonathan arriva de Jizreël. Sa nourrice le prit et s’enfuit, mais dans sa précipitation, l’enfant tomba et resta infirme. Il s’appelait Mephibosheth.)
fr.R: (Jonathan, le fils de Saül, avait un fils qui était infirme des pieds. Il avait cinq ans quand la nouvelle est arrivée de Jizreël : Saül et Jonathan avaient été tués. Sa nourrice l’a pris dans ses bras et s’est enfuie. Mais comme elle se dépêchait, l’enfant est tombé, et depuis, il ne pouvait plus marcher normalement. Il s’appelait Mephibosheth.)

sw.L: (Yonathani mwana wa Sauli alikuwa na mwana aliyelemaa miguu. Alikuwa mwana wa miaka mitano habari za Sauli na Yonathani zilipofika kutoka Yezreeli, na yaya wake akamchukua akakimbia; ikawa alipokuwa akiharakisha kukimbia, akaanguka akawa kiwete. Na jina lake [lilikuwa] Mefiboshethi.)
sw.B: (Yonathani mwana wa Sauli alikuwa na mwana aliyelemaa miguu yote miwili. Alikuwa na umri wa miaka mitano habari za Sauli na Yonathani zilipofika kutoka Yezreeli. Yaya wake alimchukua akakimbia, lakini alipokuwa akiharakisha kukimbia, mtoto akaanguka akawa kiwete. Jina lake lilikuwa Mefiboshethi.)
sw.R: (Yonathani mwana wa Sauli alikuwa na mwana aliyekuwa na miguu iliyolemaa. Alikuwa na umri wa miaka mitano habari zilipofika kutoka Yezreeli kwamba Sauli na Yonathani wameuawa. Yaya wake alimchukua akakimbia. Lakini alipokuwa akiharakisha kutoroka, mtoto akaanguka, na tangu hapo hakuweza kutembea vizuri. Jina lake lilikuwa Mefiboshethi.)

vi.L: (Giô-na-than con trai Sau-lơ có một con trai bị tật ở chân. Cậu được năm tuổi khi tin về Sau-lơ và Giô-na-than từ Gít-rê-ên đến; người vú nuôi bế cậu lên và chạy trốn; nhưng trong lúc vội vã chạy trốn, cậu bị ngã và trở nên què. Tên cậu [là] Mê-phi-bô-sết.)
vi.B: (Giô-na-than con trai Sau-lơ có một con trai bị què cả hai chân. Cậu được năm tuổi khi tin tức về Sau-lơ và Giô-na-than từ Gít-rê-ên đưa đến. Người vú nuôi bế cậu lên và chạy trốn, nhưng vì vội vã chạy, cậu bị ngã và bị què. Tên cậu là Mê-phi-bô-sết.)
vi.R: (Giô-na-than con trai Sau-lơ có một con trai bị tật ở chân. Khi tin Sau-lơ và Giô-na-than tử trận từ Gít-rê-ên đưa đến, cậu được năm tuổi. Người vú nuôi bế cậu chạy trốn. Nhưng trong lúc vội vã chạy, cậu bị ngã, và từ đó cậu không đi đứng bình thường được nữa. Tên cậu là Mê-phi-bô-sết.)

decisions.choice: the verse is an aside that interrupts the story
alternatives: the verse explains why the murderers chose to kill Ish-bosheth and not another heir
decisions.reason: The story of Ish-bosheth's death stops for a note about Jonathan's son, then goes on in verse 5. The note shows that once Ish-bosheth was gone, the only one left of Saul's line through Jonathan was a lame boy, who could not lead an army or claim the throne. It also prepares for David's kindness to him (9:1-13).

decisions.choice: the report from Jezreel: the news of Saul's and Jonathan's death
decisions.reason: Israel had camped by the spring in Jezreel before the battle on Mount Gilboa, where Saul and Jonathan died (1 Samuel 29:1; 31:1-6). The household fled when the news came, fearing the Philistines or a rival for the throne.

decisions.choice: stricken of feet ... became lame: crippled in both feet from the fall
decisions.reason: The words for "feet" are dual, "both feet". The same description returns in 9:3, 13 and 19:27.

decisions.choice: Mephibosheth: called Merib-baal in Chronicles
decisions.reason: 1 Chronicles 8:34 and 9:40 call Jonathan's son Merib-baal. As with Ish-bosheth (see 2:8), Samuel puts "bosheth", "shame", in place of "baal".

decisions.choice: parentheses around the whole verse
decisions.reason: Every level sets the aside in parentheses so that the reader sees the story pause and then resume in verse 5.

decisions.choice: the news ... that Saul and Jonathan had been killed
decisions.reason: Readable says what the news was, which the Hebrew leaves to the reader of 1 Samuel 31.

decisions.choice: the boy is "cậu" in the narration
decisions.reason: A child of a noble house, spoken of kindly; "cậu" keeps both his youth and his rank.

source.text: וַיֵּ֨לְכ֜וּ בְּנֵֽי־רִמּ֤וֹן הַבְּאֵֽרֹתִי֙ רֵכָ֣ב וּבַעֲנָ֔ה וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ כְּחֹ֣ם הַיּ֔וֹם אֶל־בֵּ֖ית אִ֣ישׁ בֹּ֑שֶׁת וְה֣וּא שֹׁכֵ֔ב אֵ֖ת מִשְׁכַּ֥ב הַֽצָּהֳרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And went [the] sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, and came in [the] heat of the day to [the] house of Ish-bosheth, and he [was] lying [the] lying of the noon.

en.L: And the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, went and came in the heat of the day to the house of Ish-bosheth, while he was lying down [for] the noon rest.
en.B: Rechab and Baanah, sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, went off and reached Ish-bosheth's house in the heat of the day, while he was taking his midday rest.
en.R: Rechab and Baanah, the sons of Rimmon from Beeroth, set out for Ish-bosheth's house. They got there in the hottest part of the day, when he was lying down for his rest at noon.

es.L: Y fueron los hijos de Rimón el beerotita, Recab y Baaná, y llegaron en el calor del día a la casa de Isboset, mientras él estaba acostado [para] el descanso del mediodía.
es.B: Recab y Baaná, hijos de Rimón el beerotita, se pusieron en camino y llegaron a casa de Isboset en lo más caluroso del día, mientras él dormía la siesta.
es.R: Recab y Baaná, los hijos de Rimón de Beerot, salieron hacia la casa de Isboset. Llegaron a la hora de más calor del día, cuando él estaba acostado descansando al mediodía.

fr.L: Et les fils de Rimmôn le Béérothite, Rékab et Baana, partirent et arrivèrent dans la chaleur du jour à la maison d’Ishbosheth, alors qu’il était couché [pour] le repos de midi.
fr.B: Rékab et Baana, fils de Rimmôn le Béérothite, se mirent en route et arrivèrent à la maison d’Ishbosheth au plus chaud du jour, pendant qu’il faisait sa sieste de midi.
fr.R: Rékab et Baana, les fils de Rimmôn de Béeroth, sont partis vers la maison d’Ishbosheth. Ils y sont arrivés au moment le plus chaud de la journée, quand il était couché pour se reposer à midi.

sw.L: Wana wa Rimoni Mbeerothi, Rekabu na Baana, wakaenda wakafika wakati wa joto la mchana kwenye nyumba ya Ishboshethi, naye alikuwa amelala [kwa] pumziko la adhuhuri.
sw.B: Rekabu na Baana, wana wa Rimoni Mbeerothi, walikwenda wakafika nyumbani kwa Ishboshethi wakati wa joto la mchana, alipokuwa akipumzika adhuhuri.
sw.R: Rekabu na Baana, wana wa Rimoni wa Beerothi, walianza safari kwenda nyumbani kwa Ishboshethi. Walifika saa za joto kali la mchana, alipokuwa amelala kupumzika adhuhuri.

vi.L: Các con trai của Rim-môn người Bê-ê-rốt là Rê-cáp và Ba-a-na đi đến nhà Ích-bô-sết vào lúc trời nóng nhất trong ngày, khi ông đang nằm nghỉ trưa.
vi.B: Rê-cáp và Ba-a-na, con trai của Rim-môn người Bê-ê-rốt, lên đường và đến nhà Ích-bô-sết vào lúc nắng gắt trong ngày, khi ông đang nghỉ trưa.
vi.R: Rê-cáp và Ba-a-na, con trai của Rim-môn người Bê-ê-rốt, lên đường đến nhà Ích-bô-sết. Họ đến nơi vào lúc nóng nhất trong ngày, khi ông đang nằm nghỉ trưa.

decisions.choice: the noon rest: the usual time to lie down in the heat
decisions.reason: People rested through the hottest hours (Genesis 18:1). The house would be quiet and the king off guard.

decisions.choice: Ish-bosheth: Saul's son, made king by Abner
decisions.reason: The name is written as two words here. On the name and its form Eshbaal, see 2:8.

decisions.choice: taking his midday rest (Balanced); lying down for his rest at noon (Readable)
decisions.reason: Hebrew says "lying the lying of noon". Balanced and Readable say it once in plain words.

source.text: וְ֠הֵנָּה בָּ֜אוּ עַד־תּ֤וֹךְ הַבַּ֨יִת֙ לֹקְחֵ֣י חִטִּ֔ים וַיַּכֻּ֖הוּ אֶל־הַחֹ֑מֶשׁ וְרֵכָ֛ב וּבַעֲנָ֥ה אָחִ֖יו נִמְלָֽטוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And there they came into [the] middle of the house, taking wheat, and struck him into the belly; and Rechab and Baanah his brother escaped.

en.L: And they came there into the middle of the house, fetching wheat, and they struck him in the belly; and Rechab and Baanah his brother escaped.
en.B: They came into the inner part of the house as though to fetch wheat, and they stabbed him in the belly. Then Rechab and his brother Baanah escaped.
en.R: They went into the house as if they had come to get some wheat. They stabbed Ish-bosheth in the stomach, and then Rechab and his brother Baanah got away.

es.L: Y allí entraron hasta el medio de la casa, tomando trigo, y lo hirieron en el vientre; y Recab y Baaná su hermano escaparon.
es.B: Entraron hasta el interior de la casa como si fueran a buscar trigo, y lo apuñalaron en el vientre. Luego Recab y su hermano Baaná escaparon.
es.R: Entraron en la casa como si hubieran venido a buscar trigo. Apuñalaron a Isboset en el estómago, y después Recab y su hermano Baaná huyeron.

fr.L: Et ils entrèrent là jusqu’au milieu de la maison, prenant du blé, et ils le frappèrent au ventre ; et Rékab et Baana son frère s’échappèrent.
fr.B: Ils pénétrèrent à l’intérieur de la maison comme pour chercher du blé, et ils le frappèrent au ventre. Puis Rékab et son frère Baana s’échappèrent.
fr.R: Ils sont entrés dans la maison en faisant semblant de venir chercher du blé. Ils ont frappé Ishbosheth au ventre avec un poignard, puis Rékab et son frère Baana se sont enfuis.

sw.L: Wakaingia huko katikati ya nyumba, wakichukua ngano, wakampiga tumboni; na Rekabu na Baana ndugu yake wakaponyoka.
sw.B: Waliingia ndani ya nyumba kana kwamba wanakuja kuchukua ngano, wakamchoma tumboni. Kisha Rekabu na ndugu yake Baana wakatoroka.
sw.R: Waliingia ndani ya nyumba kana kwamba wamekuja kuchukua ngano. Wakamchoma Ishboshethi tumboni, kisha Rekabu na ndugu yake Baana wakatoroka.

vi.L: Họ vào tận giữa nhà, [như] để lấy lúa mì, rồi đâm vào bụng ông; rồi Rê-cáp và Ba-a-na em mình trốn thoát.
vi.B: Họ vào bên trong nhà như thể đến lấy lúa mì, rồi đâm vào bụng ông. Sau đó Rê-cáp và em là Ba-a-na trốn thoát.
vi.R: Họ vào trong nhà như thể đến lấy lúa mì. Họ đâm vào bụng Ích-bô-sết, rồi Rê-cáp và em là Ba-a-na trốn thoát.

decisions.choice: the Hebrew is followed; the ancient Greek translation tells this verse differently
alternatives: the doorkeeper was cleaning wheat and fell asleep, and the brothers slipped in (ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation reads, "And look, the doorkeeper of the house was cleaning wheat, and she grew drowsy and slept; and Rechab and Baanah the brothers slipped in." That reading explains how the men got past the door and does not tell the killing twice. The Hebrew is harder: it says the men came in "taking wheat" and struck him, and verse 7 then tells the killing again. Reviewers should check the Greek wording.

decisions.choice: taking wheat: probably a pretext for entering the house
alternatives: they went in to where the wheat was kept
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has only a participle, "taking wheat". It most likely means the men came in as if to collect wheat, perhaps rations for their troops, and so drew no notice. It may simply say where in the house they went, to the place where grain was kept.

decisions.choice: in the belly: the same wound that killed Asahel and Abner
decisions.reason: Abner struck Asahel in the belly (2:23), and Joab struck Abner in the same place (3:27). The third killing of the war comes the same way.

decisions.choice: as though to fetch wheat (Balanced); as if they had come to get some wheat (Readable); stabbed
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the pretext reading explicit, and say "stabbed" for "struck" since the wound was in the belly. This goes a little beyond the bare participle.

decisions.choice: "[như] để lấy lúa mì" (L); "như thể đến lấy lúa mì" (B, R); Baanah is Rechab's "em"
decisions.reason: The wheat was probably a pretext (meaning decision), so Literal brackets "như". Vietnamese must choose older or younger brother; Rechab is named first in verses 5-6, so Baanah is taken as the younger, though verse 2 names him first.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ הַבַּ֗יִת וְהֽוּא־שֹׁכֵ֤ב עַל־מִטָּתוֹ֙ בַּחֲדַ֣ר מִשְׁכָּב֔וֹ וַיַּכֻּ֨הוּ֙ וַיְמִתֻ֔הוּ וַיָּסִ֖ירוּ אֶת־רֹאשׁ֑וֹ וַיִּקְחוּ֙ אֶת־רֹאשׁ֔וֹ וַיֵּֽלְכ֛וּ דֶּ֥רֶךְ הָעֲרָבָ֖ה כָּל־הַלָּֽיְלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they came [into] the house, and he [was] lying on his bed in [the] chamber of his lying, and they struck him and killed him and removed his head; and they took his head and went [the] way of the Arabah all the night.

en.L: And they came into the house while he was lying on his bed in his bedchamber, and they struck him and killed him and removed his head; and they took his head and went [by the] way of the Arabah all the night.
en.B: They had entered the house while he lay on his bed in his bedroom, and they struck him down, killed him, and cut off his head. Taking the head with them, they traveled all night by the road through the Arabah.
en.R: They had come into the house while Ish-bosheth was lying on his bed in his bedroom. They attacked him and killed him, and they cut off his head. Then they took the head and traveled all night along the road through the Jordan Valley.

es.L: Y entraron en la casa mientras él estaba acostado sobre su cama en su alcoba, y lo hirieron y lo mataron y le quitaron la cabeza; y tomaron su cabeza y anduvieron [por el] camino del Arabá toda la noche.
es.B: Habían entrado en la casa mientras él estaba acostado en su cama, en su dormitorio, y lo hirieron, lo mataron y le cortaron la cabeza. Llevándose la cabeza, viajaron toda la noche por el camino del Arabá.
es.R: Habían entrado en la casa mientras Isboset estaba acostado en su cama, en su dormitorio. Lo atacaron y lo mataron, y le cortaron la cabeza. Después se llevaron la cabeza y viajaron toda la noche por el camino del valle del Jordán.

fr.L: Et ils entrèrent [dans] la maison alors qu’il était couché sur son lit dans sa chambre à coucher, et ils le frappèrent et le tuèrent et lui ôtèrent la tête ; et ils prirent sa tête et marchèrent [par le] chemin de l’Araba toute la nuit.
fr.B: Ils étaient entrés dans la maison pendant qu’il dormait sur son lit, dans sa chambre, et ils l’avaient frappé, tué, puis décapité. Emportant sa tête, ils marchèrent toute la nuit par la route de l’Araba.
fr.R: Ils étaient entrés dans la maison pendant qu’Ishbosheth était couché sur son lit, dans sa chambre. Ils l’ont attaqué et tué, et ils lui ont coupé la tête. Puis ils ont pris la tête et ont marché toute la nuit sur la route de la vallée du Jourdain.

sw.L: Wakaingia nyumbani, naye alikuwa amelala kitandani mwake katika chumba chake cha kulala, wakampiga wakamwua wakaondoa kichwa chake; wakakichukua kichwa chake wakaenda [kwa] njia ya Araba usiku kucha.
sw.B: Walikuwa wameingia nyumbani alipokuwa amelala kitandani katika chumba chake cha kulala, wakampiga, wakamwua, wakamkata kichwa. Wakakichukua kichwa hicho, wakasafiri usiku kucha kwa njia ya Araba.
sw.R: Walikuwa wameingia nyumbani Ishboshethi alipokuwa amelala kitandani mwake katika chumba chake cha kulala. Wakamshambulia, wakamwua, wakamkata kichwa. Kisha wakachukua kichwa hicho, wakasafiri usiku kucha kwa njia inayopita katika Bonde la Yordani.

vi.L: Họ vào nhà khi ông đang nằm trên giường trong phòng ngủ, đánh ông, giết ông và chặt lấy đầu ông; họ mang đầu ông đi theo đường A-ra-ba suốt đêm.
vi.B: Họ đã vào nhà khi ông đang nằm trên giường trong phòng ngủ, đâm chết ông và chặt đầu ông. Họ mang đầu ông theo và đi suốt đêm theo đường qua vùng A-ra-ba.
vi.R: Họ đã vào nhà khi Ích-bô-sết đang nằm trên giường trong phòng ngủ. Họ tấn công và giết ông, rồi chặt đầu ông. Sau đó họ mang cái đầu đi suốt đêm theo con đường qua thung lũng Giô-đanh.

decisions.choice: the verse goes back over the killing and tells it more fully
decisions.reason: Verse 6 gave the deed in brief; verse 7 returns to the moment they came in and adds where he lay, that they cut off his head, and how they left. Hebrew stories often tell an event first in short and then in full.

decisions.choice: they cut off his head: to carry proof of the king's death
decisions.reason: A head was taken as proof that an enemy was dead (1 Samuel 17:51, 54; 31:9). The men meant to show it to David and claim a reward.

decisions.choice: the way of the Arabah: the road down the Jordan Valley
decisions.reason: The Arabah is the deep valley of the Jordan and the Dead Sea. Ish-bosheth's capital was Mahanaim, east of the Jordan (2:8, 12, 29). The men followed the valley south through the night before climbing to Hebron.

decisions.choice: bedroom; cut off his head; the Jordan Valley (Readable)
decisions.reason: "The chamber of his lying" is his bedroom, and "removed his head" means cut it off. Readable explains the Arabah as the Jordan Valley. Balanced and Readable say "had entered" because the verse looks back to verse 6.

source.text: וַ֠יָּבִאוּ אֶת־רֹ֨אשׁ אִֽישׁ־בֹּ֥שֶׁת אֶל־דָּוִד֮ חֶבְרוֹן֒ וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ אֶל־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ הִנֵּֽה־רֹ֣אשׁ אִֽישׁ־בֹּ֗שֶׁת בֶּן־שָׁאוּל֙ אֹֽיִבְךָ֔ אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּקֵּ֖שׁ אֶת־נַפְשֶׁ֑ךָ וַיִּתֵּ֣ן יְ֠הוָה לַֽאדֹנִ֨י הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ נְקָמוֹת֙ הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה מִשָּׁא֖וּל וּמִזַּרְעֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And they brought [the] head of Ish-bosheth to David [at] Hebron and said to the king, Here [is the] head of Ish-bosheth son of Saul, your enemy, who sought your life; and has given Yahweh to my lord the king vengeance this day from Saul and from his offspring.

en.L: And they brought the head of Ish-bosheth to David [at] Hebron and said to the king, "Look, the head of Ish-bosheth son of Saul, your enemy, who sought your life! And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given my lord the king vengeance this day on Saul and on his offspring."
en.B: They brought Ish-bosheth's head to David at Hebron and told the king, "Look, here is the head of Ish-bosheth son of Saul, your enemy, the one who sought your life. This day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given my lord the king vengeance on Saul and his descendants."
en.R: They brought the head to David at Hebron and said to him, "Look! This is the head of Ish-bosheth, the son of Saul, your enemy who tried to kill you. Today {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has paid back Saul and his family for you, my lord the king."

es.L: Y trajeron la cabeza de Isboset a David [en] Hebrón y dijeron al rey: «¡He aquí la cabeza de Isboset hijo de Saúl, tu enemigo, que buscaba tu vida! Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha dado hoy a mi señor el rey venganza de Saúl y de su descendencia».
es.B: Llevaron la cabeza de Isboset a David en Hebrón y le dijeron al rey: «Mira, aquí está la cabeza de Isboset hijo de Saúl, tu enemigo, el que buscaba quitarte la vida. Hoy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le ha concedido a mi señor el rey venganza sobre Saúl y sus descendientes».
es.R: Llevaron la cabeza a David en Hebrón y le dijeron: «¡Mira! Esta es la cabeza de Isboset, el hijo de Saúl, tu enemigo que trató de matarte. Hoy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} les ha dado su merecido a Saúl y a su familia por ti, mi señor el rey».

fr.L: Et ils apportèrent la tête d’Ishbosheth à David [à] Hébron, et dirent au roi : « Voici la tête d’Ishbosheth fils de Saül, ton ennemi, qui cherchait ta vie ! Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a donné aujourd’hui à mon seigneur le roi vengeance de Saül et de sa descendance. »
fr.B: Ils apportèrent la tête d’Ishbosheth à David, à Hébron, et dirent au roi : « Voici la tête d’Ishbosheth, fils de Saül, ton ennemi, celui qui en voulait à ta vie. Aujourd’hui, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a vengé mon seigneur le roi de Saül et de ses descendants. »
fr.R: Ils ont apporté la tête à David, à Hébron, et ils lui ont dit : « Regarde ! Voici la tête d’Ishbosheth, le fils de Saül, ton ennemi, qui voulait te tuer. Aujourd’hui, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a puni Saül et sa famille pour toi, mon seigneur le roi. »

sw.L: Wakamletea Daudi kichwa cha Ishboshethi [huko] Hebroni, wakamwambia mfalme, "Tazama, kichwa cha Ishboshethi mwana wa Sauli, adui yako, aliyekutafuta roho yako! Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amempa bwana wangu mfalme kisasi leo juu ya Sauli na juu ya uzao wake."
sw.B: Walimletea Daudi kichwa cha Ishboshethi huko Hebroni, wakamwambia mfalme, "Tazama, hiki ni kichwa cha Ishboshethi mwana wa Sauli, adui yako, aliyekuwa akitafuta kukuua. Leo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amempa bwana wangu mfalme kisasi juu ya Sauli na wazao wake."
sw.R: Walikileta kichwa kwa Daudi huko Hebroni wakamwambia, "Tazama! Hiki ni kichwa cha Ishboshethi mwana wa Sauli, adui yako aliyejaribu kukuua. Leo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amemlipa Sauli na jamaa yake kwa ajili yako, bwana wangu mfalme."

vi.L: Họ đem đầu Ích-bô-sết đến cho Đa-vít [tại] Hếp-rôn và tâu với vua: "Kìa, đầu của Ích-bô-sết con trai Sau-lơ, kẻ thù của vua, là kẻ đã tìm hại mạng sống vua! Hôm nay {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã báo thù cho chúa tôi là vua trên Sau-lơ và trên dòng dõi người."
vi.B: Họ đem đầu Ích-bô-sết đến cho Đa-vít tại Hếp-rôn và tâu với vua: "Đây là đầu của Ích-bô-sết con trai Sau-lơ, kẻ thù của bệ hạ, là kẻ đã tìm giết bệ hạ. Hôm nay {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã báo thù cho bệ hạ trên Sau-lơ và dòng dõi người."
vi.R: Họ đem cái đầu đến cho Đa-vít tại Hếp-rôn và nói với vua: "Kìa! Đây là đầu của Ích-bô-sết, con trai Sau-lơ, kẻ thù của đức vua, kẻ đã tìm cách giết đức vua. Hôm nay {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã báo trả Sau-lơ và gia đình người thay cho đức vua."

decisions.choice: your enemy, who sought your life: it may be Ish-bosheth or Saul
alternatives: Saul, your enemy, who sought your life
decisions.reason: The words can describe Ish-bosheth or his father. It was Saul who hunted David to kill him (1 Samuel 20:1; 23:15; 25:29), and the men's last words name Saul. The ambiguity is kept.

decisions.choice: Yahweh has given vengeance: the murderers claim God's approval for their deed
decisions.reason: They present the murder as Yahweh's justice on Saul's house for wronging David. David will answer with an oath in Yahweh's name that Yahweh, not they, rescued him (verse 9), and he refuses their claim.

decisions.choice: vengeance from Saul and his offspring: full payment for what Saul's house did
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is plural, "vengeances", which stresses that the score is settled completely. "Offspring" (literally "seed") means Saul's descendants and his royal line.

decisions.choice: has paid back Saul and his family for you
decisions.reason: Readable says what "given vengeance" means: Yahweh has repaid Saul's house on David's behalf.

decisions.choice: "tâu" for speaking to the king (L, B)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese has a verb for speaking up to a king; Literal and Balanced use it for subjects addressing David, Readable keeps the plain "nói".

source.text: וַיַּ֨עַן דָּוִ֜ד אֶת־רֵכָ֣ב׀וְאֶת־בַּעֲנָ֣ה אָחִ֗יו בְּנֵ֛י רִמּ֥וֹן הַבְּאֵֽרֹתִ֖י וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֑ם חַי־יְהוָ֕ה אֲשֶׁר־פָּדָ֥ה אֶת־נַפְשִׁ֖י מִכָּל־צָרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And answered David Rechab and Baanah his brother, [the] sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and said to them, [As] lives Yahweh, who has ransomed my life from all distress,

en.L: And David answered Rechab and Baanah his brother, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and said to them, "[As] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, who has ransomed my life from all distress,

decisions.choice: as Yahweh lives: a solemn oath
decisions.reason: David calls on the living God as witness to what he will say and do (1 Samuel 14:39). The oath governs the whole speech to the end of verse 11.

decisions.choice: who has ransomed my life from all distress: Yahweh, not these men, has saved David
decisions.reason: The verb means to set free, as by paying a price. David will give the same oath on his deathbed (1 Kings 1:29). He answers their claim in verse 8: Yahweh has always rescued him and needs no murder to do it.

decisions.choice: rescued; every trouble
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "rescued" for "ransomed", the plain sense here, and "as surely as ... lives" for the bare oath.

decisions.choice: two sentences, with "I give you my solemn word" supplied
decisions.reason: Readable puts the description of Yahweh first and states the oath as a sentence of its own, so that the long sentence of verses 9-11 can be broken into short ones.

decisions.choice: Aussi vrai que le SEIGNEUR est vivant
decisions.reason: For the whole of 2 Samuel, the oath "As the LORD lives" takes the form the Samuel terms note sets; Literal brackets the words French supplies.

decisions.choice: "Vive el SEÑOR" (L); "tan cierto como que el SEÑOR vive" (B, R)
decisions.reason: For the whole of 2 Samuel, the oath "As the LORD lives" takes the wording the Samuel terms note sets: the short Hebrew formula at Literal, the full sentence at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: Kama BWANA aishivyo
decisions.reason: The oath "As the LORD lives" is "Kama BWANA aishivyo", as set for Samuel in Swahili.

decisions.choice: "Thật như CHÚA hằng sống"
decisions.reason: The Samuel terms note's form for the oath; Readable keeps it after its own short sentence, as the English does.

records.literal_gloss: for the [one] telling to me, saying, Look, has died Saul, and he was like [one] bringing good news in his eyes, and I seized him and killed him in Ziklag, which [was] to give to him [for] news;

en.L: when the one telling me, saying, 'Look, Saul is dead,' was in his own eyes like one bringing good news, I seized him and killed him in Ziklag, which [was] my giving to him [a reward for] news,
en.B: when the man who told me, 'Look, Saul is dead,' thought he was bringing good news, I seized him and put him to death in Ziklag. That was the reward I gave him for his news,
en.R: Once a man came to me and said, 'Saul is dead.' He thought he was bringing me good news. But I seized him and put him to death in Ziklag. That was the reward I gave him for his news.

es.L: cuando el que me informó, diciendo: “He aquí que Saúl ha muerto”, era a sus propios ojos como quien trae buenas noticias, lo agarré y lo maté en Siclag, que [fue] lo que le di [como pago por la] noticia,
es.B: cuando el hombre que me dijo: “Mira, Saúl ha muerto”, creía que traía buenas noticias, lo agarré y le di muerte en Siclag. Esa fue la recompensa que le di por su noticia,
es.R: Una vez vino un hombre y me dijo: “Saúl ha muerto”. Creía que me traía una buena noticia. Pero yo lo agarré y lo hice matar en Siclag. Esa fue la recompensa que le di por su noticia.

fr.L: celui qui m’a renseigné en disant : “Voici, Saül est mort”, et qui était à ses propres yeux comme un porteur de bonne nouvelle, je l’ai saisi et je l’ai tué à Tsiqlag, ce qui [fut] ce que je lui donnai [pour] sa nouvelle ;
fr.B: l’homme qui m’a annoncé : “Voici, Saül est mort”, croyait m’apporter une bonne nouvelle, et je l’ai saisi et fait mourir à Tsiqlag. Voilà la récompense que je lui ai donnée pour sa nouvelle,

vi.L: khi kẻ báo tin cho ta rằng: 'Kìa, Sau-lơ đã chết,' tự cho mình như người mang tin mừng, thì ta đã bắt hắn và giết hắn tại Xiếc-lác, đó là [phần thưởng] ta trao cho hắn vì tin ấy,

vi.R: Trước đây có một kẻ đến nói với ta: 'Sau-lơ đã chết.' Hắn tưởng mình đem tin vui đến cho ta. Nhưng ta đã bắt hắn và xử tử hắn tại Xiếc-lác. Đó là phần thưởng ta trao cho hắn vì cái tin ấy.

decisions.choice: the man who told David of Saul's death at Ziklag
decisions.reason: The Amalekite came to Ziklag with Saul's crown and claimed to have killed him, expecting thanks; David had him put to death (1:1-16). David now holds the two brothers to the same standard.

decisions.choice: in his own eyes: as he himself thought
decisions.reason: The man saw himself as a bearer of good news. The verb is the one used for bringing welcome news of a victory (1 Samuel 31:9).

decisions.choice: which was my giving him for news: that was his reward
alternatives: the one to whom I should have given a reward for his news
decisions.reason: The words are bitter: the reward he looked for was his death. The noun for "news" can also mean the reward given for good news.

decisions.choice: put him to death; That was the reward I gave him
decisions.reason: Balanced makes the irony plain with "reward" and keeps the sentence open into verse 11. In 1:15 David had another man carry out the killing, so "put to death" is used.

decisions.choice: the story told in short sentences
decisions.reason: Readable tells the earlier event as a short story of its own, then draws the lesson in verse 11.

records.literal_gloss: how much more when wicked men have killed a righteous man in his house on his bed! And now, shall I not require his blood from your hand and remove you from the earth?

en.L: how much more when wicked men have killed a righteous man in his own house on his bed! And now, shall I not require his blood from your hand and purge you from the earth?"
en.B: how much more when wicked men have killed an innocent man in his own house on his bed! Now then, shall I not demand his blood from your hands and wipe you from the earth?"
en.R: You are wicked men, and you have killed an innocent man in his own house, on his own bed. That is far worse! So now I will hold you responsible for his death, and I will wipe you off the earth."

sw.L: sembuse watu waovu walipomwua mtu mwenye haki ndani ya nyumba yake juu ya kitanda chake! Basi sasa, je, sitaitaka damu yake mkononi mwenu na kuwaondoa katika dunia?"

vi.L: huống chi khi những kẻ gian ác đã giết một người công chính ngay trong nhà người, trên giường người! Vậy bây giờ, ta há không đòi máu người nơi tay các ngươi và trừ khử các ngươi khỏi mặt đất sao?"
vi.B: huống chi khi những kẻ gian ác đã giết một người vô tội ngay trong nhà người, trên giường người! Bây giờ, lẽ nào ta không đòi máu người nơi tay các ngươi và diệt trừ các ngươi khỏi mặt đất sao?"
vi.R: Các ngươi là những kẻ gian ác, và các ngươi đã giết một người vô tội ngay trong nhà người, trên giường người. Việc ấy còn tệ hơn nhiều! Vậy bây giờ ta sẽ bắt các ngươi đền tội giết người, và ta sẽ diệt trừ các ngươi khỏi mặt đất."

decisions.choice: how much more: an argument from the lesser to the greater
decisions.reason: If David killed a man who only brought news of a death in battle, he must punish far more those who murdered a man in his sleep.

decisions.choice: a righteous man: one innocent of any crime that deserved death
decisions.reason: *Tsaddiq* here describes Ish-bosheth's standing in this matter: he had done nothing to deserve being killed. It is not a claim about his whole life. The "wicked men" are those guilty of the crime.

decisions.choice: require his blood from your hand: hold you to account for his death
decisions.reason: To "require blood" is to demand the life of a murderer for the life he took (Genesis 9:5-6; 42:22). "Remove" (literally "burn out" or "purge") is the word of the laws that remove evil from Israel (Deuteronomy 19:13, 19; 21:21).

decisions.choice: innocent man
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "innocent" because "righteous" might suggest a claim about his goodness in general. Literal keeps "righteous".

decisions.choice: the question becomes a statement
decisions.reason: Readable turns David's question, which expects the answer yes, into a firm statement, and states the comparison as "That is far worse".

decisions.choice: "người công chính" (L); "người vô tội" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Innocent of any crime deserving death (meaning decision), as the English levels have it.

records.literal_gloss: And commanded David the young men, and they killed them and cut off their hands and their feet and hanged [them] by the pool in Hebron; and [the] head of Ish-bosheth they took and buried in [the] tomb of Abner in Hebron.

en.L: And David commanded the young men, and they killed them and cut off their hands and their feet and hanged [them] beside the pool in Hebron; and they took the head of Ish-bosheth and buried [it] in the tomb of Abner in Hebron.
en.B: Then David gave orders to his young men, and they killed them. They cut off their hands and feet and hung their bodies beside the pool in Hebron. But Ish-bosheth's head they took and buried in Abner's tomb at Hebron.
en.R: Then David gave orders to his soldiers, and they put the two men to death. They cut off their hands and feet and hung up their bodies beside the pool in Hebron, where everyone could see them. But they took Ish-bosheth's head and buried it in Abner's tomb in Hebron.

es.L: Y dio David órdenes a los jóvenes, y los mataron y les cortaron las manos y los pies y [los] colgaron junto al estanque en Hebrón; y la cabeza de Isboset la tomaron y [la] sepultaron en el sepulcro de Abner en Hebrón.
es.B: Entonces David dio órdenes a sus jóvenes, y ellos los mataron. Les cortaron las manos y los pies y colgaron sus cuerpos junto al estanque de Hebrón. Pero la cabeza de Isboset la tomaron y la sepultaron en el sepulcro de Abner en Hebrón.
es.R: Entonces David dio órdenes a sus soldados, y ellos mataron a los dos hombres. Les cortaron las manos y los pies y colgaron sus cuerpos junto al estanque de Hebrón, donde todos pudieran verlos. Pero tomaron la cabeza de Isboset y la enterraron en la tumba de Abner, en Hebrón.

fr.L: Et David donna des ordres aux jeunes gens, et ils les tuèrent, et leur coupèrent les mains et les pieds, et [les] pendirent près de l’étang à Hébron ; et ils prirent la tête d’Ishbosheth et [l’]ensevelirent dans le tombeau d’Abner à Hébron.
fr.B: Alors David donna l’ordre à ses jeunes gens, et ils les tuèrent. Ils leur coupèrent les mains et les pieds et pendirent leurs corps près de l’étang d’Hébron. Quant à la tête d’Ishbosheth, ils la prirent et l’ensevelirent dans le tombeau d’Abner à Hébron.
fr.R: Ensuite David a donné des ordres à ses soldats, et ils ont tué les deux hommes. Ils leur ont coupé les mains et les pieds et ils ont pendu leurs corps près de l’étang d’Hébron, là où tout le monde pouvait les voir. Mais ils ont pris la tête d’Ishbosheth et l’ont enterrée dans le tombeau d’Abner à Hébron.

sw.L: Daudi akawaamuru vijana, wakawaua, wakakata mikono yao na miguu yao, wakawatundika kando ya bwawa huko Hebroni; na kichwa cha Ishboshethi wakakichukua wakakizika katika kaburi la Abneri huko Hebroni.
sw.B: Kisha Daudi aliwaamuru vijana wake, nao wakawaua. Wakakata mikono na miguu yao, wakaitundika miili yao kando ya bwawa huko Hebroni. Lakini kichwa cha Ishboshethi walikichukua wakakizika katika kaburi la Abneri huko Hebroni.
sw.R: Kisha Daudi akawaamuru askari wake, nao wakawaua wale watu wawili. Wakakata mikono na miguu yao, wakaitundika miili yao kando ya bwawa huko Hebroni ambapo kila mtu angeiona. Lakini kichwa cha Ishboshethi walikichukua wakakizika katika kaburi la Abneri huko Hebroni.

vi.L: Đa-vít truyền lệnh cho các thanh niên, và họ giết chúng, chặt tay chân chúng và treo [xác] bên ao tại Hếp-rôn; còn đầu Ích-bô-sết thì họ lấy đem chôn trong mộ Áp-ne tại Hếp-rôn.
vi.B: Rồi Đa-vít ra lệnh cho các thanh niên của mình, và họ giết hai kẻ ấy. Họ chặt tay chân chúng và treo xác chúng bên ao tại Hếp-rôn. Còn đầu Ích-bô-sết thì họ lấy đem chôn trong mộ Áp-ne tại Hếp-rôn.
vi.R: Rồi Đa-vít ra lệnh cho binh lính của mình, và họ xử tử hai kẻ ấy. Họ chặt tay chân chúng và treo xác chúng bên ao tại Hếp-rôn để mọi người đều thấy. Còn đầu Ích-bô-sết thì họ đem chôn trong mộ Áp-ne tại Hếp-rôn.

decisions.choice: the young men: David's fighting men
decisions.reason: *Ne'arim* can mean servants or young soldiers; here they act on the king's orders, as in 2:14 and 1:15.

decisions.choice: cut off their hands and feet and hanged them: a public mark of disgrace
alternatives: the hands and feet were cut off only to disgrace the bodies
decisions.reason: Hanging a body in public showed that the dead man had been put under a curse and served as a warning (Deuteronomy 21:22-23; Joshua 10:26). Cutting off the hands that did the killing and the feet that ran with the head may have marked the crime. Hebron's pool was a public place, so all who came would see that David had no part in the murder.

decisions.choice: buried in Abner's tomb: an honorable burial
decisions.reason: Abner had been buried at Hebron with David mourning him (3:31-32). Ish-bosheth's head was laid with the man who had made him king.

decisions.choice: his young men; his soldiers (Readable); their bodies; where everyone could see them (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whose men these were and that the bodies were hung. Readable names the young men as soldiers and adds that the bodies were on public view, which the place and the custom imply.
